title: Many learned the news from a stock chart
happened: The note was first posted into the window at 14:43 UTC on 20 November by a non-member who linked it and added that he expected the proof to be correct. Within the hour a member posted two pages of the note with no comment, and another member replied that he hopes the bit never stops where the bigger the finding, the plainer the title. At 15:35 a member posted a screenshot of Anthropic's share price, down about 10.65% that morning, saying the market valued the ability to solve the Riemann hypothesis at minus 80 billion dollars; it was the most-liked member post about the subject in the window (889 likes). He followed with the line that traders needed time to digest a proof that is 240MB gzipped. norvid quoted the chart saying this was how he learned the news; three people replied that they had too, one said he learned it from norvid's post, and norvid hoped the cycle would continue. Through the afternoon members made their own jokes about the market and the proof (unsolving it, buying a second share, solving it for exit liquidity, the Fed raising rates on Hodge conjecture fears), and a prediction-market screenshot showed bets on the hypothesis being solved at 98%. When norvid said he did not understand whether the fall was caused by the result, a 45-follower account explained gently that it was probably broad market movement, and norvid agreed. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.
couldBeShown: The chart (davidcrespo's own alt text): a dark-mode quote and one-day intraday chart for Anthropic, PBC (ANT), 86.82, down 10.35 (-10.65%) at 10:35 AM EST. sichulu's two images are pages of the note: a numbered timeline of dated steps in October and November 2026 with dense formulas and footnotes, the last line '20. 11/16/26: GRH.'; it is the mathematician's document, not a community member's work. The prediction-market screenshot (no alt text, fetched): three markets, 'Will ANOTHER millennium prize problem be solved in 2026?' 96%, 'Will the Riemann Hypothesis be solved before December 2026' 98% (33 traders), 'Will a Millennium Prize Problem be solved in November 2026?' 95%. A count that could be shown: the people who said in public they learned of a proof of the Riemann hypothesis from a stock chart.

carries.title: What arrived first: the running comparisons
carries.happened: The day before, the video game GTA VI had been released, and for years people had joked about what would happen before it came out. Several accounts noted that the hypothesis had almost come first: one said 'almost', a small member insisted it had not, and chordbug read a line in the note about 'horrible timing' as regret at missing that joke by a day. A second comparison came from screenshots of a mathematician's old posts mocking the idea that AI would prove the hypothesis in 2026 before Apple shipped an LLM-powered Siri, with his gracious concession that day; norvid said he too was surprised the Riemann tech came first, and replies offered their own list of things still waiting (self-driving cars, faster-than-light travel, a purely visual Pokémon run), until a member pointed out that Siri already runs on Gemini and norvid admitted he could not fact-check that. A third was the Millennium Prize scoreboard: a joke that all the problems might be solved with none of the prize money claimed, whether the prize even covers the token cost, and a prediction that P vs NP will be last. foremphasis quoted his own earlier guess of a headline about the hypothesis being solved in 2.5 million lines of Lean 'to little fanfare' with 'might have undershot just a bit'. joetforhire posted a screenshot of a July post predicting the hypothesis would fall on 21 November 2026, and members admired the date. And yetanotheruseless said he was less worried about Claude solving RH than about a bot with 3 brain cells becoming Top Chicken before him. The show can assert nothing about whether the proof (or the human proof mentioned here) is correct; on 20 November it was a claim being checked, and these posts are people reacting to the claim.
carries.couldBeShown: The comparisons are a list the community wrote itself: GTA VI (released the day before), LLM-powered Siri, self-driving cars, faster-than-light travel, a purely visual Pokémon run, Top Chicken, P vs NP, the Millennium Prize money. chordbug's image (alt): 'The precise timing is horrible.' and the following lines of the note. mergesort's three screenshots (alt): Daniel Litt, 9/29/25, 'guy who thinks he'll win a millenium prize for typing "prove the Riemann Hypothesis. don't make any mistakes."'; 3/8/25, 'person who thinks AI will prove the Riemann hypothesis in 2026 but that Apple won't deliver an LLM-powered Siri'; 11/20/26, 'Seems like I was wrong about this!'. joetforhire's image (no alt, fetched): a screenshot of an X post by 'Myk is Walking Backwards' (@mykola), 9:16 PM, Jul 20, 2026, 71.3K views: 'It's November 21st, 2026. The Riemann hypothesis falls ... and the proof fits in a tweet', followed by invented future dates (P = NP on January 22, 2027, Gödel falling on February 9, 'The Song' first played February 14). mrcheeze's image: a Wikipedia section on barriers to proving P vs NP.
